title: CSV has twelve columns in exact order, is flat (customer then invoice rows), and follows the blank-cell rules
permissions_required: Sales By Customer report View permission.
preconditions: 1. You have downloaded the CSV for a view with at least one customer with several invoices.
steps: 2. Read a customer row and an invoice row.
expected: 1. The CSV has twelve columns in this exact order: Customer, Invoice #, Date, Inv. Hrs, Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin, Shop Supplies, Margin, Margin %, Subtotal.
2. On customer rows the Invoice # and Date cells are blank.
3. On invoice rows the Customer cell is blank and the Invoice # and Date cells are filled.
4. Customer names are plain — the "(N)" invoice count is not included.
5. The CSV is flat — Customer then Invoice rows; the on-screen asset layer is NOT represented (this is per spec, not a defect).
design_ref: none - SPEC-ONLY (Report Suite has no designs yet)
spec_ref: specs/sbc-sales-by-customer.md Story 14 S14-R6; S14-R7; S14-R8; S14-R9; S14-R10 (context note)
notes: KNOWN-LIMITATION ENCODING: no asset layer in the CSV is by design (S14-R10 context note) — do not file it as a gap.
